description:
## Goal

Make every current source producer calculate, validate, and publish one complete typed contribution batch without mutating authoritative World values before the batch is accepted.

A batch is one actual publication event, not a whole-program pass and not a promise that every later macro-generated declaration is known up front.

## Authority and boundary

- The proposed batch contains every declaration body, reference, expectation, semantic owner, provenance version, fact claim, and changed-value decision produced by that event.
- Validate conflicts for every domain represented in the batch before any proposed claim becomes visible.
- Apply a valid batch once to the existing World domain stores and ordinary job claim ledger. The batch is transient completion data, never a retained second value authority.
- Parse/index/surface validation determines whether a candidate source version may be accepted. Work that inherently requires compiled same-source macros happens after acceptance as an ordinary dependent derivation; its failure is completed by `fz-tfn.46`, not mislabeled as pre-acceptance rejection.
- A same-source item macro may consume accepted declarations through ordinary facts/products, but proposed current-batch definitions are never exposed provisionally to unrelated consumers.

Do not compare before/after World images, copy accepted state, stage a second World, retain a shadow owner map, reconstruct writes, or roll back mutations that have already escaped.

## Absorbed law

This cut absorbs `fz-kdt.79`: typed callsite value stores and their `CallSiteSummary`/`CallSiteTargets` fact claims have one lifetime. Last-publisher retraction removes the value; later `Unresolved` publication starts a fresh epoch and cannot inherit stale `Resolved` content. Implement that at the unified publication boundary, not as per-reader presence shims or after-the-fact repair.

## TDD signal

Use public production submissions and focused World tests for functions, modules, types, structs, protocols/providers, specs, macros, generated declarations, requester expectations, and lazy runtime reservations. For every conflict/failure injected at each position in a multi-domain batch, either the whole batch publishes or none of it does. Facts and typed stores never disagree.

Pin the accepted module lifecycle exposed while integrating fz-tfn.62: repeated discovery of a provider already at `Defined` must not overwrite its store slot back to `Indexed` while the existing `ModuleDefined` fact remains published. A top-level `require Provider` followed by demand for an exact bound `Provider.helper/1` currently stalls because `ModuleMap::index_body` demotes the value without an equivalent fact transition. Equal rediscovery is a no-op; a real replacement publishes one coherent typed batch. This is the existing module-overwrite obligation, not a retry or a new lifecycle authority.

Prove same-source item-macro publication without candidate leakage, a second World, or self-deadlock. State explicitly which errors reject before source acceptance and which are downstream failed derivations. Preserve unchanged/unrelated zero work, lazy lowering, exact diagnostics, semantic answers, and artifacts.

## Required deletion

Delete mutation-before-validation paths, module/type overwrite paths, separate type-reference publication, append-only requester obligations, store-without-ledger test helpers, stale callsite values after retraction, rollback/reconciliation ideas, and documentation describing partial publication.

Update source, module, type, macro, fact-engine, semantic-fixpoint, and pipeline docs. Full focused/deterministic/library/fixture/CLI gates, formatting, check, and strict Clippy pass. Fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precedes one commit and close.
title: Publish validated source contributions as one typed batch
